pageCache.text:
Inspiring excellence
Vision, Ethos & Values
Our Vision
At The Vyne Community School, we are dedicated to empowering young people to aim high, believe in themselves, and achieve success—both academically and personally.
We believe that education has the power to transform lives. Every young person deserves an excellent education that develops their knowledge, broadens their horizons and gives them the confidence and ambition to shape their own future.
We are ambitious for every student, regardless of their starting point or circumstances. We believe that schools should be places of hope and opportunity: places where barriers are overcome, talents are discovered and young people begin to see what is possible for their future.
Academic success is central to this. Qualifications open doors and create choices, and we want every student to leave The Vyne with the knowledge, skills and confidence to take their next steps successfully. However, education is about more than examination results. We have an equally important responsibility to develop the character, values and sense of responsibility that will enable our young people to lead happy and fulfilling lives and make a positive contribution to their communities and the wider world.
Our DOVE Values
Our school community is united by four values:
Determination • Opportunity • Valour • Empathy
Together, they form our DOVE values and provide a shared understanding of the qualities we want to develop in every member of our community.
They are not simply words. They influence how we learn, how we treat one another, how we respond when things are difficult and the expectations we have of ourselves and others.
Determination
We embrace challenge, persevere and strive to be our best.
Success requires effort, resilience and the willingness to keep going when something is difficult.
We encourage our students to approach challenges positively, learn from mistakes and understand that improvement comes through purposeful effort. We develop independent learners who take responsibility for their choices, their learning and their future.
Determination means having the confidence to set ambitious goals and the perseverance to pursue them.
Opportunity
We participate, aim high and make the most of every opportunity.
We want every student to experience an education that expands their horizons and increases the choices available to them.
Opportunity begins with access to a broad, ambitious curriculum and excellent teaching, but it extends far beyond the classroom. Through our co-curricular programme, careers education, leadership, sport, the arts, Combined Cadet Force, trips, visits and experiences beyond school, we encourage students to discover new interests, develop their talents and imagine possibilities for themselves that they may not previously have considered.
We recognise that opportunity is not always equally available. We therefore work actively to understand and remove barriers so that every student can participate, achieve and thrive.
Valour
We have the courage to do what is right.
Valour means acting with courage, integrity and personal responsibility.
We encourage students to develop the confidence to make good decisions, stand up for themselves and others, speak out when something is wrong and remain true to their values, even when doing so is difficult.
It also means accepting responsibility when we make mistakes, learning from them and having the courage to try again.
We want our students to become principled young adults who understand that leadership is not simply about being in charge; it is about having the character to act with integrity and contribute positively to the lives of others.
Empathy
We listen, understand, respect and care for others.
Strong communities are built on positive relationships.
We teach our students to recognise and value the experiences, perspectives and feelings of others. We expect every member of our community to treat others with kindness, dignity and respect and to recognise the strength that comes from difference and diversity.
Empathy does not simply mean understanding how someone else feels. It means allowing that understanding to influence how we behave.
Through empathy, our students learn that they have a responsibility not only for themselves, but also towards the people and communities around them.
Our Values in Action
Our DOVE values shape every aspect of life at The Vyne.
They can be seen in the ambition of our curriculum and the expectations we have in our classrooms; in the opportunities students have beyond their lessons; in the way students and staff treat one another; in our commitment to inclusion and removing barriers; and in the contribution our young people make to the school and wider community.
We want students to leave The Vyne with excellent qualifications, but also with much more.
We want them to leave us as knowledgeable, confident and compassionate young adults who are ambitious for their futures, resilient when they encounter challenges, courageous enough to stand up for what is right and determined to make a positive difference.
That is what it means to be part of The Vyne Community School.

Inspiring excellence
Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to The Vyne Community School.
It is a genuine privilege to serve as Headteacher of this remarkable school and to welcome you to our community. Choosing the right school is one of the most important decisions a family makes, and I hope this website gives you a sense of who we are, what we stand for and most importantly, what we aspire every child to become.
At The Vyne, we believe that education has the power to transform lives. Every young person deserves the opportunity to discover their strengths, develop confidence in themselves and leave school equipped with the knowledge, character and ambition to lead a happy, successful and fulfilling life. Our role extends far beyond examination results; we are preparing young people to contribute positively to their communities and to the wider world.
Our vision is simple: to empower every student to aim high, believe in themselves and achieve their full potential.
Everything we do is underpinned by our DOVE values:
Determination – developing resilience, independence and the confidence to embrace challenge.
Opportunity – ensuring every student has access to a rich curriculum and the experiences that broaden horizons, raise aspirations and open doors for the future.
Valour – encouraging integrity, courage and personal responsibility, so that students stand up for what is right and lead with character.
Empathy – fostering kindness, respect and compassion, enabling our students to value difference, build strong relationships and make a positive contribution to society.
These values are not simply words displayed on our walls; they shape our curriculum, our culture and our expectations. They are reflected in our classrooms, our enrichment programme, our relationships and in the way we support every member of our community to flourish.
Academic success matters enormously because it creates opportunity. Our ambitious curriculum is carefully designed to develop deep knowledge, critical thinking and a lifelong love of learning. At the same time, we know that outstanding education also develops character. Whether through leadership opportunities, sport, the arts, the Combined Cadet Force, our co-curriculum and enrichment activities or service to others, we encourage every student to discover passions, develop confidence and realise that they are capable of achieving far more than they may have imagined.
At The Vyne, we are ambitious for every child, regardless of their starting point. We believe schools should be places of hope where barriers are overcome, potential is realised and futures are changed. Our dedicated staff work tirelessly to ensure every student is known, valued and challenged to be the very best version of themselves.
Strong schools are built on strong partnerships. We value the trust that parents and carers place in us and believe that when school and home work together with shared purpose, young people thrive. Together, we can nurture not only successful learners but also compassionate, resilient and responsible citizens.
I hope you enjoy exploring our website and learning more about life at The Vyne. If you are considering joining our school, I warmly invite you to visit us. Nothing compares to seeing our vibrant community in action, meeting our students and staff, and experiencing first-hand the warmth, ambition and sense of belonging that make The Vyne such a special place.
I look forward to welcoming you.

Careers Education
Vyne Vista
Careers at The Vyne
Explore your future. Understand your options. Take your next step.
Vyne Vista is The Vyne School's careers programme. It helps every student look ahead with confidence, raise their aspirations, understand the choices available to them and take practical steps towards a future that is right for them.
What is Vyne Vista?
Vyne Vista is The Vyne School's careers programme. Its aim is to help every student look ahead with confidence, raise their aspirations, understand the choices available to them, and take practical steps towards a future that is right for them.
Through Vyne Vista, students will explore a wide range of pathways, including college, vocational courses, apprenticeships, technical qualifications, higher education and employment. They will take part in careers lessons, employer encounters, workplace experiences, college and provider events, application support, personal guidance and activities that link learning in school to life beyond The Vyne.
Our programme is planned around the Gatsby Benchmarks, helping us provide a stable, meaningful and inclusive careers offer for every year group. It reflects our DOVE values of Determination, Opportunity, Valour and Empathy, while promoting respect, aspiration, equality and the confidence to contribute positively to society.
Vyne Vista is here to support students and families at each stage of the journey, helping every young person discover possibilities, make informed choices and move forward with ambition, independence and hope.
Your Vyne Vista Journey
Students build knowledge, skills and confidence over time through lessons, tutor activities, Careers Checkpoints, employer encounters, provider events, guidance meetings and wider opportunities.
Students reflect on who they are, explore dream jobs, learn what we mean by a career, find out about entrepreneurship, consider work-life balance and begin thinking about the future of work.
Students reflect on their interests, learn about CVs and workplaces, consider what success means to them and explore how careers connect to the climate and wider world.
Students reflect on their skills, choose KS4 options, explore learning pathways after school, take control of their career journey, learn about money and explore labour market information.
Students reflect on their career journey, explore employer profiles and career types, prepare for Work Experience, learn about workplace wellbeing and begin looking ahead to post-16 pathways.
Students focus on post-16 choices, compare pathways, research paid and voluntary work, consider AI and the future of jobs, reflect on employability skills and prepare for successful transition.
Quality, Impact & Destinations
The Vyne School has achieved national recognition through the Quality in Careers Standard using the Career Mark approach provided by Complete Careers. This award reflects the school's commitment to high-quality careers education, information, advice and guidance for students.
Destination data helps us understand the next steps students take after Year 11 and how well our programme supports positive progression into education, employment or training. Published destination information should always be aggregated and anonymised.
Vyne Vista is reviewed regularly to help ensure that the programme remains effective, inclusive and relevant. We use a range of evidence to evaluate careers provision, including student voice, staff feedback, employer and provider feedback, guidance records, destination information and review against the Gatsby Benchmarks.

Our Partnership with Fujitsu
We are proud of our ongoing partnership with Fujitsu, which provides students with meaningful opportunities to learn from employers and understand how skills developed in school connect to the modern workplace.
Through this partnership, students have experienced activities such as enterprise projects, CV and interview preparation, apprenticeship awareness, workplace insight and employer-led support. These opportunities help students build confidence, develop employability skills and see the relevance of their learning beyond the classroom.
Partnerships like this are an important part of Vyne Vista because they help students connect aspiration with real examples of employment, training and progression.

Unifrog
Unifrog is an online careers and destinations platform used by students at The Vyne. It helps students explore their interests, research future pathways and understand the steps they can take to prepare for their next stage of education, training or employment.
Through Unifrog, students can explore careers, apprenticeships, college courses, university options, school leaver programmes and a range of wider enrichment opportunities. The platform also supports students with developing employability skills, recording activities, writing CVs and preparing personal statements.
Unifrog is used as part of the Vyne Vista careers programme to help students make informed decisions, keep track of their progress and build a stronger picture of their future options.

Partners
BASCITT
If you're a graduate and want to complete your training in a school environment, consider school-centred initial teacher training (SCITT). The Basingstoke Alliance SCITT delivers Initial Teacher Training programmes which have been designed and are delivered by groups of schools and colleges within Basingstoke and Deane situated in North Hampshire. The programmes are taught by experienced, practising teachers, and are tailored towards our local teaching needs. All our courses lead to qualified teacher status (QTS).
If you prefer to spend more time training in the classroom, putting theory into practice and gaining confidence through increased contact with the school environment, then a Basingstoke Alliance SCITT programme is a good option for you.
If you are interested in gaining school based experience prior to applying for a teacher training course The Vyne School runs a School Experience Programme with the Department for Education. For further information either contact Sara Kemp, Assistant Headteacher directly at The Vyne School or visit http://www.education.gov.uk/get-into-teaching/school-experience/se
Basingstoke Young Carers
The Vyne has had a long standing relationship with Basingstoke Young Carers and work closely in helping those students who need support and guidance.
A Young Carer is defined as a child or young person who is undertaking a caring role for a family member with a terminal/long term illness or disability. This also includes hard-to-reach children and young people who are affected by their parent's behaviour through drug & alcohol abuse, mental health problems or domestic violence.

Ocean Youth Trust
Over a period of 2 years The Vyne has worked closely with Ocean Youth Trust, with nearly 30 students involved in 4 Vyne Sailing voyages.
Ocean Youth Trust South is charity which uses Adventure under Sail as a personal development opportunity for young people aged 12-25, taking them to sea in their 72-foot yacht John Laing.
OYT sail with around 450 young people each year. Roughly two-thirds will be disadvantaged or vulnerable in some way: they work in partnership with other organisations both to select these young people and also to ensure that lessons learned and achievements enjoyed on a voyage are carried through into a long-term programme of work with each young person.
For all these young people, a voyage is designed to develop confidence, team-working, ability to cope with unfamiliar situations, and tolerance and understanding of others. Young crew members not only sail the boat, keep watch and help to navigate; they also learn basic life skills such as cooking and healthy eating. Sail training brings benefits to all sorts of young people, perhaps their lives are dominated by television and computer games and they really need an active outdoor adventure.

Inspiring excellence
Personal, Social and Health Education
Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education (PSHE)
Preparing Young People for Life
At The Vyne Community School, education is about preparing young people not only for examinations, but for life.
Our Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education (PSHE) curriculum helps students develop the knowledge, understanding, confidence and judgement they need to navigate the opportunities, responsibilities and challenges they will encounter as they grow into adulthood.
We want our students to leave The Vyne able to make informed decisions, build positive relationships, look after themselves and others, understand the world around them and contribute positively to their communities.
PSHE therefore plays an important role in bringing our DOVE values of Determination, Opportunity, Valour and Empathy to life.
An Ambitious Curriculum for Every Student
Our PSHE curriculum is carefully planned and sequenced from Year 7 to Year 11 so that students revisit important themes with increasing depth and maturity as they progress through the school.
Students develop their knowledge and understanding across key areas including:
Our curriculum is responsive to the world our young people are growing up in. Where appropriate, we adapt and supplement our planned curriculum to address emerging issues while ensuring that students build secure knowledge over time.
physical health and wellbeing;
emotional wellbeing and resilience;
relationships, including friendships, families and respectful relationships;
Relationships and Sex Education (RSE);
personal safety, safeguarding and recognising risk;
consent, boundaries and healthy relationships;
equality, diversity and respect;
drugs, alcohol, vaping and other risk-taking behaviours;
financial education and managing money;
careers, aspirations and preparation for the future;
citizenship, democracy and life in modern Britain;
recognising exploitation, coercion and unhealthy behaviours;
making informed, responsible decisions.
Developing Confidence and Character
PSHE gives students a safe and structured environment in which to explore important issues, consider different perspectives and develop the confidence to make informed choices.
Through discussion, reflection and carefully chosen learning activities, students are encouraged to think critically about the influences around them and consider the consequences of their decisions for themselves and others.
Our DOVE values provide an important foundation for this learning.
Determination helps students develop resilience, manage setbacks and make choices that support their long-term goals.
Opportunity encourages students to understand the possibilities available to them and develop the knowledge and confidence to make informed choices about their future.
Valour means having the courage to make the right decision, establish boundaries, resist pressure, ask for help and speak up when something does not feel right.
Empathy helps students build healthy relationships, respect difference and understand how their words, choices and actions affect other people.
Relationships and Sex Education
Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) forms an important part of our PSHE curriculum and is taught in an age-appropriate and sensitive way.
Our aim is to help students understand what healthy, respectful relationships look like and to give them the knowledge they need to keep themselves and others safe.
Students learn about areas including friendships, families, consent, boundaries, intimate relationships, sexual health, online relationships and recognising unhealthy or abusive behaviours.
We recognise the important role parents and carers play in educating their children about relationships and growing up. We therefore aim to communicate clearly about our RSE curriculum and work in partnership with families.
Further information about the content and delivery of RSE, including the school's statutory responsibilities and parents' rights, can be found in our Relationships and Sex Education Policy.
Learning to Stay Safe
An important purpose of PSHE is ensuring students have the knowledge and confidence to recognise when something may be wrong and know what to do about it.
Students learn how to identify risk, recognise potentially harmful or exploitative situations, understand appropriate boundaries and know where and how to seek help.
We want students to understand that asking for help is a strength.
We encourage our young people to look out for one another and to have the Valour to speak to a trusted adult when they are worried about themselves or somebody else.
Understanding and Respecting Others
The Vyne is a diverse and inclusive community.
Through PSHE, students learn about different identities, cultures, beliefs, families, experiences and perspectives. They are encouraged to challenge prejudice and discrimination and understand the importance of treating everyone with dignity and respect.
We want students to be able to disagree respectfully, listen to different viewpoints and develop their own opinions based on knowledge and thoughtful consideration.
This is central to our value of Empathy and to preparing young people to participate positively in modern Britain.
Looking to the Future
PSHE also helps students consider who they want to become.
Through careers education, financial education, goal setting and opportunities to explore future pathways, students are encouraged to think ambitiously about their lives beyond The Vyne.
We want every student to understand that their future is not predetermined by their starting point or circumstances. Our role is to help them develop the knowledge, confidence and aspiration to recognise opportunities and make informed choices about the next stage of their lives.
Working in Partnership
The most effective PSHE education is built on partnership between school, students, parents and carers.
We encourage families to talk to their children about the issues explored through PSHE and welcome constructive dialogue about our curriculum.
Our detailed PSHE curriculum maps show what students learn in each year group and allow parents and carers to understand how knowledge develops from Year 7 through to Year 11.
Together, we can help our young people develop the knowledge, character and confidence they need to make positive choices, build healthy relationships and approach their futures with ambition.
We want every student to leave The Vyne knowing how to keep themselves safe, how to value and respect others, and confident in their ability to make choices that will shape a positive future.

Inspiring excellence
Governors
Thank you for visiting our page and a very warm welcome form the Governors of the Vyne Community School.
So what is our role as governors?
In my view, our role is to embed ourselves into the school’s ethos; understand the needs of the whole school and establish a working relationship with the school’s head and her team to ensure open and transparent conversations can take place that ensure all aspects of school governance are carried out in a robust and fair manner. This is achieved by regular communications and committee meetings covering every aspect of school life and educational provision. This is further supported by frequent governor school visits to assess specific areas such pastoral and SEN provision. In short the governing body is there to hold the Vyne accountable for its whole school approach in a way that is fair and supportive.
Who are your governing body?
The governing body that supports the school is made of a diverse group of parent and co- opted individuals with a wide range of backgrounds and skill sets. These varied skill sets are essential in ensuring all aspects of governance are sufficiently covered with a good knowledge base. Where specific skills are identified for governors’ appropriate training is provided via Hampshire Educational Services, along with regular training to ensure the committee is up to date with any legislation changes. In summary we are a committed and passionate committee who share a common value, to ensure the Vyne is a safe, all-inclusive and open environment that provides challenging and engaging learning opportunities for your children.
Chair of Governors summary:
Being part of the governing body for the past 6 years as a co-opted governor I can honestly say that together we have achieved great success in developing the Vyne and its links with our local community. The great trust and partnership we have with the head teacher and her team ensures that we can achieve great success together which flows down to the whole school. This is something that I feel immensely proud to be part of and I hope that you feel that we have your childrens’ welfare and best interests to heart.

Inspiring excellence
Current Vacancies
Learning Support Assistant: Click Here
We are looking for enthusiastic and committed Learning Support Assistants to join our dedicated and expanding team. The people we are looking for will be able to relate well to young people and show sensitivity to pupils with learning, language and behavioural difficulties. The successful candidates must have good organisational skills; administrative and recording skills are also essential. Along with the ability to show initiative, whilst maintaining and respecting confidentiality. A willingness to undertake further training is required.
Finance Officer: Click Here
We are seeking to appoint a highly organised, motivated and experienced Finance Officer to join our friendly school team. This is an important role supporting the effective financial management of our maintained school, ensuring that resources are managed efficiently and used to support the best possible outcomes for our pupils.
Working closely with the Headteacher, Senior Leadership Team and Governing Body, the successful candidate will take responsibility for the day-to-day management of the school's finances, providing accurate financial information, effective budget monitoring and advice to support sound financial decision-making.
This part-time position offers an opportunity for an experienced finance professional to make a valuable contribution to the life and success of our school.
